courseTitle: iOS App Development & Computer Science Fundamentals

modules.title: Swift Fundamentals & Type Safety
modules.subtitle: Variables, constants, optionals, value types, and control flow in modern Swift.
modules.summary: Master the building blocks of Swift including type inference, optionals, guard statements, and collection types.

topics.title: Constants, Variables & Type Inference
topics.explanation: Swift uses `let` to declare immutable constants and `var` to declare mutable variables. Type safety ensures that values never silently convert to incompatible types, while type inference allows the compiler to deduce types automatically from initial values.
topics.keyTakeaway: Prefer `let` by default for safety and immutability; only use `var` when a value must change.
topics.codeExample:
let maxAttempts = 3
var currentScore: Int = 0
let appName = "LearnQuest" // Inferred as String

topics.title: Optionals & Safe Unwrapping
topics.explanation: An Optional (`T?`) represents either a wrapped value or `nil`. Instead of force-unwrapping with `!`, use `if let` or `guard let` bindings, or the nil-coalescing operator `??` to handle missing values safely without runtime crashes.
topics.keyTakeaway: Use `guard let` for early exits and `??` for sensible default values.

topics.title: Structs vs. Classes (Value vs. Reference Types)
topics.explanation: In Swift, `struct` and `enum` are value types (copied on assignment), whereas `class` is a reference type (shared instance managed via Automatic Reference Counting). Value types prevent unintended shared-state mutations across components.
topics.keyTakeaway: Default to structs for data models; use classes when identity or inheritance is required.

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to declare an immutable constant in Swift?
quiz.explanation: `let` declares a constant whose value cannot be reassigned after initialization.

quiz.question: What does an Optional type `String?` represent in Swift?
options: A string that is always empty
Either a valid String value or nil
quiz.explanation: Optionals explicitly model the possible absence of a value (`nil`).

quiz.question: Which operator provides a default value when an Optional is nil?
quiz.explanation: The nil-coalescing operator (`??`) unwraps an optional or returns a fallback value if it is `nil`.

quiz.question: How are Swift structs passed when assigned to a new variable?
quiz.explanation: Structs in Swift are value types and use copy-on-write semantics.

quiz.question: Why is `guard let` preferred at the start of a function?
options: It executes on a background queue
It unwraps optionals and exits early if conditions fail
quiz.explanation: `guard let` keeps the happy path unindented and guarantees unwrapped values remain in scope.

modules.title: UIKit Lifecycle & Storyboard Design
modules.subtitle: UIViewController lifecycle, Auto Layout constraints, segues, and IBOutlets.
modules.summary: Understand how UIViewControllers manage screen hierarchies, how Storyboards instantiate scenes, and how Auto Layout adapts interfaces across screen sizes.

topics.title: UIViewController Lifecycle Methods
topics.explanation: `viewDidLoad()` is called once when the view hierarchy loads into memory—ideal for initial setup and bindings. `viewWillAppear(_:)` runs every time the screen is about to become visible, making it ideal for refreshing dynamic progress state.
topics.keyTakeaway: Perform one-time layout in `viewDidLoad()` and state refreshes in `viewWillAppear(_:)`.

topics.title: Storyboards, Scenes & Identifiers
topics.explanation: Storyboards visually organize view controllers as scenes connected by segues or instantiated via `Storyboard ID`. Using `instantiateViewController(withIdentifier:)` enables passing strongly typed ViewModels while maintaining visual Storyboard design.
topics.keyTakeaway: Assign a clear Storyboard ID matching the class name for reliable instantiation.
topics.codeExample:
let storyboard = UIStoryboard(name: "Main", bundle: nil)
let vc = storyboard.instantiateViewController(withIdentifier: "QuizViewController")

topics.title: Auto Layout & Stack Views
topics.explanation: Auto Layout calculates frame positions dynamically from constraints (leading, trailing, top, bottom, width, height). `UIStackView` simplifies vertical and horizontal layouts by managing child constraints automatically.
topics.keyTakeaway: Always set `translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false` when adding programmatic constraints.

quiz.question: Which lifecycle method is called only once when the view controller's view is first loaded into memory?
quiz.explanation: `viewDidLoad()` runs once after the view controller loads its view hierarchy.

quiz.question: What property must be set to `false` when applying programmatic Auto Layout constraints?
quiz.explanation: Disabling `translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints` prevents conflicting autoresizing mask constraints.

quiz.question: Which UIKit container arranges subviews linearly along a horizontal or vertical axis?
quiz.explanation: `UIStackView` manages layout constraints automatically for a vertical or horizontal stack of views.

quiz.question: How do you instantiate a specific scene from `Main.storyboard` in code?
quiz.explanation: `instantiateViewController(withIdentifier:)` creates an instance of the scene matching the Storyboard ID.

quiz.question: Why are `@IBOutlet` properties typically declared as `weak`?
options: To avoid strong reference cycles with the view hierarchy
quiz.explanation: The view controller's root `view` already holds a strong reference to its subviews.

modules.title: Mastering UITableView & Cell Reuse
modules.subtitle: DataSource, Delegate, cell dequeueing, dynamic row heights, and pull-to-refresh.
modules.summary: Build smooth, high-performance scrolling lists using UITableView cell reuse queues, custom cells, and automatic self-sizing rows.

topics.title: UITableViewDataSource & UITableViewDelegate
topics.explanation: `UITableViewDataSource` supplies the data (number of sections, rows, and configured cells), while `UITableViewDelegate` handles user interaction (row selection, swipe actions, and custom header views).
topics.keyTakeaway: Separate data population (`DataSource`) from user interaction (`Delegate`).

topics.title: Cell Reuse Queue & Performance
topics.explanation: Instead of allocating hundreds of views simultaneously, `dequeueReusableCell(withIdentifier:for:)` recycles off-screen cells as the user scrolls. Always reset stateful subviews inside your cell's `configure` method.
topics.keyTakeaway: Register custom cells once in `viewDidLoad()` and dequeue them by reuse identifier.

topics.title: Self-Sizing Cells with Automatic Dimension
topics.explanation: By setting `tableView.rowHeight = UITableView.automaticDimension` and providing a complete top-to-bottom chain of Auto Layout constraints inside `contentView`, `UITableView` computes dynamic row heights automatically.
topics.keyTakeaway: Pin the top-most subview to `contentView.topAnchor` and bottom-most subview to `contentView.bottomAnchor`.

quiz.question: Which protocol method is required by `UITableViewDataSource`?
quiz.explanation: `numberOfRowsInSection` and `cellForRowAt` are the two required `UITableViewDataSource` methods.

quiz.question: How does `dequeueReusableCell(withIdentifier:for:)` improve scrolling performance?
options: It pre-renders the entire table into an image
It recycles cell instances that scroll off-screen instead of allocating new views
It runs UI rendering on a background thread
quiz.explanation: Reusing existing cell allocations keeps memory usage low and frame rates at 60/120 FPS.

quiz.question: What is required for `UITableView.automaticDimension` to calculate cell height accurately?
options: Implementing heightForRowAt with a fixed CGFloat
An unbroken chain of vertical Auto Layout constraints from contentView top to bottom
Using fixed frame rects in layoutSubviews
quiz.explanation: Auto Layout needs continuous vertical constraints between `contentView.topAnchor` and `contentView.bottomAnchor`.

quiz.question: Which `UITableViewDelegate` method handles a user tapping on a module row?
quiz.explanation: `tableView(_:didSelectRowAt:)` is triggered when a user taps a row.

quiz.question: Which control is attached to `tableView.refreshControl` to support pull-to-refresh?
quiz.explanation: `UIRefreshControl` provides native pull-to-refresh behavior in `UITableView` and `UIScrollView`.

modules.title: MVVM Architecture in iOS
modules.subtitle: Separating Models, Views, and ViewModels for testable, maintainable apps.
modules.summary: Learn how Model-View-ViewModel eliminates Massive View Controllers by isolating presentation logic, state transformation, and service calls inside ViewModels.

topics.title: Roles of Model, View, and ViewModel
topics.explanation:
In MVVM:
• Model holds domain data structs (`LearningModule`, `UserProgress`).
• View / ViewController renders UI and forwards user actions.
• ViewModel transforms Model data into display-ready strings/progress values and coordinates API & storage services.
topics.keyTakeaway: ViewModels should never `import UIKit` or reference `UIView` subclasses directly.

topics.title: Data Binding via Closures & Delegation
topics.explanation: Views observe ViewModel state updates using lightweight closure callbacks (`onDataUpdated`), `Combine`, or protocols. Remember to capture `[weak self]` inside closures stored by the ViewModel to avoid retain cycles.
topics.keyTakeaway: Always use `[weak self]` when binding ViewController callbacks to a ViewModel.

topics.title: Dependency Injection & Unit Testing
topics.explanation: By passing service protocols (`APIServiceProtocol`, `LocalStorageServiceProtocol`) into a ViewModel's initializer with default shared instances, you can easily inject mock services during unit tests without network or disk side effects.
topics.keyTakeaway: Depend on protocols rather than concrete singletons for clean testability.

quiz.question: In MVVM architecture, which layer is responsible for formatting model data for display?
quiz.explanation: The ViewModel transforms raw domain Models into presentation-ready values for the View.

quiz.question: Why should a ViewModel avoid importing `UIKit`?
options: To keep the ViewModel decoupled from UI classes and easily unit-testable
Because Swift files cannot import UIKit
quiz.explanation: Keeping ViewModels independent of UIKit ensures clean separation of concerns and fast unit tests.

quiz.question: What capture list prevents memory leaks when binding a closure in a ViewController to its ViewModel?
quiz.explanation: `[weak self]` breaks the strong reference cycle between the ViewController and the ViewModel.

quiz.question: How does protocol-based Dependency Injection help when testing a ViewModel?
options: It allows injecting mock API and storage services in unit tests
quiz.explanation: Injecting protocol abstractions allows tests to supply deterministic mock responses.

quiz.question: Which responsibility belongs in `UIViewController` under MVVM?
options: Parsing raw JSON data from URLSession
Rendering UI subviews and forwarding user taps to the ViewModel
quiz.explanation: In MVVM, the ViewController acts as part of the View layer, handling layout and user input events.

modules.title: Local Data Storage & Codable Persistence
modules.subtitle: Saving XP, badges, and progress with UserDefaults, Codable, and FileManager.
modules.summary: Persist student progress, high scores, and cached learning modules across app launches using Swift's Codable protocol, UserDefaults, and the Documents directory.

topics.title: Encoding & Decoding with Codable
topics.explanation: Swift's `Codable` typealias combines `Encodable` and `Decodable`. Using `JSONEncoder` and `JSONDecoder`, complex nested structs (`UserProgress`, `LearningModule`) serialize cleanly to and from `Data`.
topics.keyTakeaway: Conform model structs to `Codable` for automatic JSON serialization.
topics.codeExample:
let data = try JSONEncoder().encode(progress)
let decoded = try JSONDecoder().decode(UserProgress.self, from: data)

topics.title: UserDefaults for Lightweight State
topics.explanation: `UserDefaults.standard` stores user preferences and lightweight serialized state (such as `UserProgress` XP and completed module IDs) in a key-value plist managed by iOS.
topics.keyTakeaway: Use reverse-DNS keys (e.g., `com.learnquest.userProgress.v3`) to avoid key collisions.

topics.title: FileManager & the Sandbox Documents Directory
topics.explanation: For larger datasets such as cached syllabus JSON files, store data inside the app sandbox's `.documentDirectory` or `.cachesDirectory` using `data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)` to prevent partial writes.
topics.keyTakeaway: Use `.atomic` file writes so corrupted files are never left behind if interrupted.

quiz.question: What two protocols are combined by the `Codable` typealias in Swift?
quiz.explanation: `typealias Codable = Decodable & Encodable`.

quiz.question: Which class converts a `Codable` Swift struct into JSON `Data`?
quiz.explanation: `JSONEncoder` encodes any `Encodable` value into JSON `Data`.

quiz.question: What is `UserDefaults` best suited for storing?
options: Lightweight user preferences and progress metadata
quiz.explanation: `UserDefaults` is ideal for preferences and small state objects like user progress.

quiz.question: What does the `.atomic` option do when writing `Data` to a file URL?
options: Writes to a temporary file first and renames it to prevent partial corruption
Compresses the file into a zip archive
Uploads the file to iCloud automatically
quiz.explanation: Atomic writing ensures the destination file is either completely written or left untouched.

quiz.question: How do you locate a bundled JSON file such as `modules.json` inside the app bundle?
quiz.explanation: `Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)` locates resources packaged inside the app target.

modules.title: Web Services with URLSession
modules.subtitle: REST API requests, HTTP status validation, JSON decoding, and main-thread UI dispatch.
modules.summary: Integrate remote web services using URLSession, validate HTTP responses, decode JSON payloads, and safely update UIKit components on the main thread.

topics.title: Creating & Resuming URLSession Data Tasks
topics.explanation: `URLSession.shared.dataTask(with:completionHandler:)` creates an asynchronous network request. Tasks start in a suspended state, so calling `.resume()` is mandatory to initiate the HTTP request.
topics.keyTakeaway: Never forget to call `task.resume()` after creating a `URLSessionDataTask`.

topics.title: Validating HTTP Status Codes & Decoding
topics.explanation: Before decoding the response body, cast `URLResponse` to `HTTPURLResponse` and verify `(200...299).contains(httpResponse.statusCode)`. Then decode the JSON payload using `JSONDecoder`.
topics.keyTakeaway: Always check for a 2xx HTTP status code before attempting JSON decoding.

topics.title: Dispatching UI Updates to the Main Queue
topics.explanation: `URLSession` completion handlers execute on a background queue. Because all `UIKit` updates must occur on the main thread, wrap completion callbacks in `DispatchQueue.main.async { ... }`.
topics.keyTakeaway: Always hop back to `DispatchQueue.main.async` before updating UIKit views or reloading `UITableView`.

quiz.question: Why does a newly created `URLSessionDataTask` not start immediately?
options: Tasks are created in a suspended state and require calling `.resume()`
It waits for the user to tap the screen
URLSession only runs when connected to Xcode
quiz.explanation: All `URLSessionTask` instances begin suspended; calling `.resume()` starts execution.

quiz.question: On which thread/queue does `URLSession`'s `dataTask` completion handler run by default?
quiz.explanation: `URLSession` executes completion handlers on a background queue to avoid blocking the UI.

quiz.question: How must you update `UITableView` after receiving network data in a `URLSession` callback?
quiz.explanation: UIKit is not thread-safe; all UI mutations must be dispatched to the main queue.

quiz.question: Which HTTP status code range indicates a successful web service response?
quiz.explanation: HTTP 2xx status codes (such as 200 OK) indicate success.

quiz.question: Why is an offline fallback cache useful alongside `URLSession` in an educational app?
options: It lets students continue studying and taking quizzes even without an internet connection
It replaces the need for UIViewControllers
quiz.explanation: Caching syllabus modules locally ensures uninterrupted learning offline.
